name: Bathysphere Networks
sector: Subsurface & Underwater Infrastructure, Deep Telecom & Lakebed Resource Extraction
employees: 95,000 direct; 200,000 contracted subsurface construction and maintenance workers
sovereign_territory: The Bathysphere Deep Territories — legally claimed lakebed zones across Lakes Erie, Huron, and Michigan totaling approximately 12,000 square kilometers of subsurface sovereign space, plus the Bathysphere Hub, a pressurized underwater operations complex 40 meters below the surface of Lake Michigan near former Chicago's northern shore.
founding_story: The sovereignty question of Great Lakes lakebeds was legally ambiguous for decades after the collapse of federal and state governance structures. In 2139, maritime engineer and legal scholar Dr. Tomasz Wroblewski-Fane filed a 3,000-page sovereignty claim on behalf of his newly incorporated Bathysphere Networks, arguing that the lakebed territories were unclaimed sovereign space under the emerging GLMZ Corponation Sovereignty Accords. After four years of legal combat, he won a partial claim in 2143 that established the precedent for subsurface sovereignty. Bathysphere immediately began laying the infrastructure — deep telecom cables, subsurface pipelines, and lakebed resource extraction systems — that made their territorial claim economically meaningful. The Bathysphere Hub, completed in 2149, is the only permanently staffed underwater corponation facility in the Great Lakes.
security_force: The Depth Guard — 8,000 personnel, the majority of whom are submarine and underwater drone operators rather than conventional soldiers. Bathysphere's security posture is almost entirely focused on subsurface threat response: protecting cable infrastructure, lakebed extraction sites, and the Hub itself from sabotage and rival extraction operations. Surface intrusions are handled by a smaller rapid-response marine unit. The Depth Guard operates a fleet of 34 autonomous submersibles.
key_detail: Bathysphere controls the primary subsurface telecom cable network connecting the eastern and western zones of GLMZ. Saltmarsh Telecom's surface network and Bathysphere's deep network are technically complementary but commercially competitive. Bathysphere has quietly positioned itself so that any serious disruption to Saltmarsh's surface infrastructure would make Bathysphere's subsurface network the only viable alternative — a contingency that Bathysphere's strategic planning division refers to internally as 'the inheritance.'
relationship_to_big_20: Bathysphere is a Big 20 member and occupies a uniquely unassailable position due to the physical inaccessibility of most of their sovereign territory. Saltmarsh Telecom regards them as a long-term existential threat to surface telecom dominance. Dredge Mining Collective has contested Bathysphere's lakebed extraction rights in three separate arbitration proceedings, losing each time. Kelpline Logistics uses Bathysphere's subsurface cable infrastructure under a lucrative licensing agreement that Bathysphere has repeatedly threatened to revoke during contract negotiations.
full_text: Bathysphere Networks Sovereign Corponation, Ltd. (BSPH-N) claims sovereignty over 12,000 square kilometers of Great Lakes lakebed — the most unusual territorial configuration of any corponation in GLMZ. Founded in 2139 by maritime engineer and legal scholar Dr. Tomasz Wroblewski-Fane through a landmark sovereignty claim on legally ambiguous lakebed territories, Bathysphere spent four years in legal combat before securing the precedent-setting ruling that established subsurface sovereign rights under the GLMZ Corponation Sovereignty Accords. The infrastructure buildout that followed — deep telecom cables, subsurface pipelines, lakebed mineral extraction systems — transformed a legal abstraction into a Φ3.4 trillion enterprise generating Φ580 billion annually. The Bathysphere Hub, a pressurized underwater operations complex 40 meters below Lake Michigan's surface, serves as corporate headquarters and a symbol of the corponation's radical commitment to its subsurface identity. Ninety-five thousand direct employees and 200,000 contractors maintain the vast web of underwater infrastructure that makes Bathysphere indispensable to GLMZ's connectivity. The Depth Guard, an 8,000-strong force built around submarine warfare and autonomous submersible operations, protects assets that surface-based military forces cannot easily threaten. Bathysphere's long game — the strategic positioning of their deep cable network as the inevitable successor to Saltmarsh's surface infrastructure — is the most carefully constructed corponation contingency plan in the corridor. Wroblewski-Fane, now 67 and reportedly unwilling to work above water for more than 48 consecutive hours, remains CEO.
